question: On 23 June 2026, the Commission, together with several Member States, welcomed a Taliban delegation in Brussels to discuss migration issues, notably the return of Afghan migrants to their home country. The Commission explained that these were merely technical discussions. It also points out that the EU does not formally recognise the Taliban regime and continues to condemn the numerous violations of fundamental rights, especially the restrictions on women and girls. 1.
What concrete results were achieved at that meeting, in particular as regards the return of Afghan nationals subject to a return decision?

Does the continuation of these discussions depend on Afghanistan’s de facto authorities cooperating fully with a view to readmitting Afghan nationals subject to return decisions and combating illegal migration networks?
What steps is the Commission taking to ensure that these contacts are not perceived as being a formal recognition or political legitimisation of the Taliban regime?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.8.2026) 1. On 23 June 2026, Commission and Sweden, on behalf of interested Member States, cochaired a technical meeting in Brussels with representatives of the de facto authorities of Afghanistan responsible for return and readmission.

The meeting followed a letter sent in October 2025 by 20 Ministers from Member States and Schengen associated countries who asked the Commission to coordinate at EU level technical contacts on return and readmission to Afghanistan, with a focus on persons who pose a threat to public order and national security.

The discussion contributed to clarifying technical aspects of the different stages of the readmission procedure. 2. There are no concrete plans at this stage for further engagement on this topic with the Afghan de facto authorities at EU level. 3.

When the Taliban returned to power in August 2021, the EU adopted a policy of principled engagement with them, as ratified by Council conclusions of September 20211 and March 20232. The EU maintains diplomatic presence in Kabul and speaks to the Afghan de facto authorities in a principled way, without recognising or legitimising them in any manner, on issues pertaining to its key values and interests.

The aforementioned technical meeting on returns was within the parameters of the EU’s principled engagement policy. It implies no change in the EU’s policy of not recognising and not legitimising the Afghan de facto authorities.
